result.rule: Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use standard loop or multi-instance characteristics only when repetition is explicit; choose sequential or parallel instances from the description.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

args.text: When the description explicitly distinguishes preparation or self-assessment from a subsequent external review or audit, model the external review as a separate activity.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing learned guideline already covers the potentially omitted audit activity.

result.rule: When the description says a request is evaluated against stated criteria before an approval decision.: Model the evaluation as a separate activity before the approval decision.

When the description presents multiple distinct activities as optional alternatives: Model each activity separately on an appropriate branch, rather than combining the alternatives into one activity, and preserve their connection to the subsequent flow.
When the description states that an additional activity may be performed.: Model that activity on an optional branch, preserving its connection to the subsequent flow.
When the description states that an action has mutually exclusive alternatives for how or where it is carried out: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway and a separate task for each alternative.

args.text: When the description distinguishes preparatory work or a self-assessment from a later external review, model the external review as a separate activity before modeling the findings identified during that review.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing learned guideline already covers the separate external-review activity indicated by the missing-element record.

result.rule: When the description says a request is evaluated against stated criteria before an approval decision.: Model the evaluation as a separate activity before the approval decision.

When the description says that a process may continue only after an external participant approves a proposal: Model the approval wait as an intermediate catch event after the proposal is provided and before the dependent activity; preserve that order rather than modeling the wait as a task.
When the description states that an additional activity may be performed.: Model that activity on an optional branch, preserving its connection to the subsequent flow.

When the description says that feedback from reviews may prompt repeated changes to a proposed outcome.: Model feedback handling as a distinct activity, then use a decision point to route the flow through the relevant change and review work again when needed, or onward when no further change is needed.
